bus_p3_joel: A new roommate doesn't win you over with a speech on move-in day (hopefully, right?). The rent just has to keep showing up. Your Protector, the grown-up you, earns that protective part's trust about the same way, mostly out in ordinary life. The things you do can be small, like keeping a promise to yourself nobody else knew about. Or saying no to someone, and not texting an hour later to take it back. That second one can be really hard.
bus_last_w2_first_half: That part doesn't have to move out. It can keep watch while you take one small step toward your little one, as long as you're still present and could stop. I'd rather have it there than pretend it's gone. If it says no to that step, I'd take the no. If it lets you, watch that part for any change, even a small one.
bus_last_w2_second_half: A critic that kept calling all this stupid might turn out to be scared of getting its hopes up. I wouldn't want to get mine up either. You can answer that fear right away: "You don't have to hope yet. I'll keep coming back, even when I mess up." It might be the first time it's heard that from you.
